statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail 10 sits in the low band while Stress 47 remains elevated; the narrow danger window spans 12:30Z-15:00Z.
recommendation: The deterministic mapping holds at EA_ON because Tail remains in the low band after a fourth consecutive hour of overnight-range containment and a completed fade off the post-earnings high. The forward path lifts Tail into the WATCH band only for the 13:00Z and 14:00Z hours covering the U.S. cash open and the first full cash hour of NVIDIA repricing, and the published danger window stays confined to 12:30Z-15:00Z rather than covering the whole session.
headline: Post-NVIDIA spike fully faded inside an unchanged overnight band: Tail holds at 10, Stress eases to 47 into the claims and cash-open window
body: Nasdaq-100 September futures trade at 29,472.75, up 183.25 points or 0.63%, as of 05:16Z against a previous close of 29,289.50. The central observation of this assessment is that the overnight range of 29,432.50 to 29,654.75 is now unchanged for a fourth consecutive clock-hour, and that price has retraced roughly 182 points from the post-earnings spike high to sit in the lower third of that band without printing a new low. That is the opposite of the pattern this framework treats as dangerous. There has been no shallow-pullback sequence, no failed retracement followed by repeated extension, and no holding near a session extreme; instead the initial impulse has been given back in an orderly way while the band held. Regional trade tells the same story. The Nikkei 225 stands at 66,211.70, down 0.08%, after opening at 66,775.78 and travelling a wide 65,782.59 to 66,954.69 band before settling back near its lower end - a fade and partial recovery rather than an aligned one-way risk impulse. The catalyst behind the overnight gap is verified: NVIDIA reported second-quarter fiscal 2027 revenue of 96.2 billion dollars, up 106% year on year, with data-centre revenue of 89.0 billion dollars, up 117%, and guided third-quarter revenue to 108.0 billion dollars plus or minus 2%, above the roughly 104.2 billion dollar consensus. Cross-assets are notably unaligned rather than stacked. VIX closed at 14.89, down 6.00% on the day, with the whole session confined to 14.77 to 15.95. WTI is 81.71 dollars, down 0.63% and lower for a fourth consecutive session on reported Middle East diplomatic progress, which removes rather than adds an energy amplifier. Treasury yields are firmer but orderly, with the 10-year at 4.66% and the 2-year at 4.23%, both up under a basis point. The one genuine conflict is inflation: July PCE prices rose 0.2% on the month and 3.7% on the year, with core at 0.2% and 3.3%, and the headline annual rate ran above the 3.6% consensus. A firmer yield path and a hotter headline inflation print sitting alongside an equity market pricing an AI capital-expenditure upgrade widens the distribution of outcomes, which is a Stress condition rather than a Tail condition. Wednesday's cash session also closed slightly lower, with the Nasdaq-100 index at 29,995.38, down 0.17%, and megacap performance split three to five, so the overnight gap has not yet been ratified by a cash auction. That unratified gap, not the earnings result itself, is the reason the forward path lifts Tail into the WATCH band for the two hours covering the 13:30Z cash open. The published danger window is confined to 12:30Z to 15:00Z, spanning initial jobless claims and the opening repricing. Shared Finviz cross-asset context was read but is roughly 190 minutes old at assessment time, beyond the 90-minute freshness threshold, so it was treated as stale and not relied upon; all levels cited here come from independent primary-source research.

lookbackSummary: Over the preceding 24 hours Claude held Tail in the 10-16 band through the Wednesday European and U.S. sessions, with Stress drifting from 52 up to 61 as the market positioned into July PCE and the NVIDIA print. Tail stepped to 21 for the 20:00Z hour containing the earnings release, then decayed through 18, 16, 13, 12, 11 and 10 as the reaction proved two-sided rather than one-way. Two hourly slots, 21:00Z on 26 August and 00:00Z on 27 August, have no published Claude assessment and are marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: The forward window holds Tail in the 10-12 band across the remaining Asian and European hours on the observation that the overnight range has now contained four consecutive hours and the post-earnings spike has already been given back. It rises to 15 for the hour containing initial jobless claims at 12:30Z and to 20 for the cash-open hour and the first full cash hour, which is the only stretch mapped to WATCH, then decays back to 10 through the U.S. afternoon and the overnight session before a small lift into the Friday Jackson Hole keynote. The published danger window is confined to 12:30Z-15:00Z. Every forecast value beyond the current clock-hour is conditional risk rather than observed structure, and the escalation conditions named in each hour are shallow or absent pullbacks, repeated extension after a failed retracement, and NQ holding near a session extreme.

forecast.analysis: Observed: NQ Sep trades 29,472.75, up 0.63%, and the overnight band of 29,432.50-29,654.75 is unchanged for a fourth clock-hour. Price has faded about 182 points off the post-earnings high and sits near the lower third of that band, so retracement is occurring rather than one-way extension.

drivers: Asian session close-out, thin transition liquidity before Europe
Invalidation checkpoint: sustained acceptance below 29,432.50
WTI 81.71 down 0.63% for a fourth session, energy amplifier absent

forecast.analysis: European cash open. The overnight NVIDIA gap has not yet been tested by a large-volume auction, so a modest conditional lift is applied. A one-way European impulse that holds NQ near a session extreme would be the first genuine Tail amplifier of the day; a rotation back inside the band would not.
drivers: European cash open auction repricing the overnight gap
Checkpoint: whether NQ holds near a session extreme after the open
Megacap tape was mixed on Wednesday, three of eight higher

forecast.analysis: First full European hour. Scores stay in the low Tail band on the assumption that the contained band behaviour persists. Stress edges up because a firmer yield backdrop, with 10-year at 4.66% and 2-year at 4.23%, sits against an equity market pricing an AI capital-expenditure upgrade.
drivers: 10-year 4.66% and 2-year 4.23%, firmer but orderly
Yield firmness against equity strength is a conflict, not an amplifier
Conditional: repeated extension after a failed pullback would lift Tail

forecast.analysis: Mid-morning European trade. The published path assumes continued two-sided rotation inside the overnight band. Conflicting cross-asset signals normally widen the distribution of outcomes and raise Stress while leaving the mean-reversion-failure probability that Tail measures broadly unchanged.
drivers: Conflicting cross-asset signals widen dispersion, raising Stress
Semiconductor tape was split on Wednesday, ARM and QCOM up, NVDA down
No aligned yields, oil, volatility and breadth stack observed so far

forecast.analysis: Pre-U.S. positioning begins. Stress continues to drift up ahead of the 12:30Z data block. This remains conditional: nothing in the current evidence establishes the persistent directional efficiency that a mean-reversion failure would require, and hypothetical post-release alignment is not counted as observed.

Event importance raises Stress and lowers Confidence before Tail

forecast.analysis: Final hour before the U.S. data block. A small conditional Tail step reflects the standard thinning of two-sided liquidity into a scheduled release, not any observed structural change. The overnight band remains the reference; a clean break with follow-through would be the escalation trigger.
drivers: Liquidity thins into the scheduled 12:30Z release
Reference band remains 29,432.50-29,654.75 until broken with follow-through
Jackson Hole symposium under way, Warsh keynote is a Friday checkpoint

Tail rises only modestly because a first-instance data reaction that retraces is the ordinary case, as the 7 August payrolls episode showed.

First-instance data whipsaw normally retraces rather than trending
Danger window opens at 12:30Z

The 4 August failure began from an aligned regime at the open, so opening-auction continuation with shallow pullbacks is the specific pattern being guarded against.

Opening-auction continuation with shallow pullbacks is the guarded pattern

If instead the open produces a normal rotation with genuine retracements, these published scores would prove conservative.

forecast.analysis: U.S. lunchtime lull. Volume normally thins and directional conviction fades, which historically supports mean reversion. The conditional risk here is a low-liquidity drift that later extends, so the named checkpoint is whether pullbacks during the lull remain proportionate to the preceding move.
drivers: Lunchtime volume lull typically supports mean reversion
Watch that pullbacks stay proportionate to the preceding move

forecast.analysis: Early U.S. afternoon. The published Tail returns to the low band on the assumption that the day's two scheduled catalysts are fully absorbed by this point and no delayed second information wave is pending, unlike the multi-stage central-bank sequences that require broader protection.
drivers: Scheduled U.S. catalysts absorbed, no delayed second wave pending
No multi-stage central-bank sequence scheduled for Thursday
